entries.title: LiFePO4 (LFP) vs NMC lithium-ion
entries.summary: DRAFT. Per BU-205: LFP 3.2-3.3 V, 90-120 Wh/kg, 2000+ cycles, thermal runaway 270 C; NMC 3.6-3.7 V, 150-220 Wh/kg, 1000-2000 cycles, 210 C.

entries.title: Phosphate found as a lithium battery cathode (1996)
entries.summary: DRAFT. BU-205 states that in 1996 the University of Texas and other contributors discovered phosphate as a cathode material for rechargeable lithium batteries.

entries.title: Lithium (Li, element 3)
entries.summary: DRAFT. Lithium (Li, atomic number 3) has NIST standard atomic weight [6.938, 6.997] and naturally occurring isotopes Li-6 and Li-7. USGS tracks global lithium mineral commodity supply and demand, centered on rechargeable battery production.

entries.title: Copper (Cu, element 29)
entries.summary: DRAFT. Copper (Cu, atomic number 29) has NIST standard atomic weight 63.546(3) and stable isotopes Cu-63 and Cu-65. Per USGS, high ductility, thermal and electrical conductivity, and corrosion resistance make copper the third most consumed industrial metal, with electrical uses accounting for roughly three quarters of demand.

entries.title: Iron (Fe) and steel alloys
entries.summary: DRAFT. Iron (Fe, atomic number 26) has NIST standard atomic weight 55.845(2). Per USGS, steel is iron alloyed with a small amount of carbon, and iron and steel together account for about 95 percent of all metal tonnage produced annually worldwide.

entries.title: Commodity plastics and polymer resins
entries.summary: DRAFT. EPA materials-specific data tracks major polymer resins in packaging and durable goods, including polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles, high-density polyethylene (HDPE) containers, low-density polyethylene (LDPE) films, and polystyrene food-service items.

entries.title: Silica, glassmaking sand, and high-purity quartz
entries.summary: DRAFT. USGS classifies silica into industrial sand and gravel (used in glassmaking and foundry work), high-purity quartz (at least 99.99% silica, used for fused quartz crucibles in semiconductors), industrial quartz crystal, silica stone, and tripoli.

entries.title: Chemical safety labels and GHS Safety Data Sheets
entries.summary: DRAFT. OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard aligns with the UN Globally Harmonized System (GHS), requiring standardized 16-section Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and chemical labels bearing a harmonized signal word, pictogram, hazard statement, and precautionary statements.

entries.title: Bell bronze (copper-tin bell metal)

tiers.everyday: Bell bronze is a hard alloy of about four parts copper to one part tin. The tin makes the metal ring, but too much makes the bell brittle and likely to crack.
tiers.student: Bell metal is a high-tin bronze: the CCCBR gives around 80% copper and 20% tin. Alloying makes the metal harder, more rigid and more elastic than either metal alone. Too much tin makes it brittle and prone to cracking. It is melted at about 1,100 °C for casting. The Liberty Bell's NPS analysis is about 70% copper and 25% tin with traces of other metals.
